target.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting
target.body:
Related: #1000
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108435
Core fix: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110382

## What This PR Does

This brings the Windows Companion setup path forward to the current OpenClaw beta track and fixes the Companion-side defects found while validating that integration:

- pin the Companion-owned installer to official OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.2`;
- make compact number labels deterministic under `pt-PT` and other decimal-comma locales;
- coordinate Gateway reload suspension/restoration around the native wizard;
- survive the expected Gateway restart and reconnect during onboarding;
- order keepalive, pairing, revocation recovery, and final setup progress correctly;
- stabilize the affected connection, E2E, and accessibility tests.

This is intentionally a beta-target PR. Maintainer approval of a prerelease default is still required; it is not presented as the stable-channel policy.

## Ownership

- The Windows Companion owns WSL creation, systemd/service lifecycle, Windows Node bootstrap, setup progress, and MXC integration.
- OpenClaw owns the native onboarding wizard and Gateway command runtime.
- The Companion uses the released `wizard.start` contract with an empty parameter object; it does not invent protocol fields.
- No OpenClaw core patch or custom package is included in this PR.

## Current-Head Validation

Final local head: `9c308f0bd13948ccfd3c39d0e7373914fa8d6801`, integrated with upstream main `4518dd87ed2bbfbdb3e1389cd88e2bc95141ea2b`.

- Full repository build: passed, zero warnings/errors.
- Connection: `443/443` passed.
- SetupEngine: `448/448` passed.
- Tray: `1742/1742` passed.
- Shared: `2866` passed; `31` explicit integration skips.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Disposable Companion-owned WSL revocation/reconnect E2E: `1/1` passed.
- Strict Gateway -> Windows Node -> MXC E2E: `2/2` passed, without skip allowance.
- Both E2E runs completed uninstall and removed their temporary WSL distros.

The supported-path proof first installed official beta.2 through the normal Companion flow. Official beta.2 then reproduced the Gateway-loss failure during the native wizard. A separately built OpenClaw package containing the narrow non-exiting wizard-runtime fix was injected only into the disposable proof distro; with that correction, revocation/reconnect and MXC both passed. That package is evidence for a separate OpenClaw PR, not hidden Companion behavior.

## Failed-First Evidence

- Earlier public CI installed official beta.2 but lost the Gateway during the wizard/reconnect path.
- The exact OpenClaw failure was isolated to wizard commands invoking the normal exiting CLI runtime inside the Gateway process.
- The separate OpenClaw fix uses a non-exiting runtime, treats only exit code zero as normal completion, and propagates nonzero exits; its focused tests pass `8/8`, and its official build/pack path passes.
- Current-head Companion E2E succeeds only after that explicit corrected-package injection. Therefore official beta.2 alone remains a known dependency blocker.

## Auto-review

The final public branch diff was reviewed with Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` at high reasoning. One P2 claimed the restart helper uninstalls the service before retrying. Direct call-path inspection rejected it: `StartOrRestartAndWaitForHealthAsync` has no uninstall call; `gateway uninstall` exists only in `InstallGatewayServiceStep.RollbackAsync`, which the restart helper does not invoke. Accepted actionable findings: zero.

## Scope And Security

- No `/new` or session behavior changes.
- No token, secret, model, memory, plugin, or agent-policy changes.
- No new permissions or network destinations.
- No broader command authority.
- No operator runtime was installed or mutated for validation.

## Review State

- [x] Current `main` integrated without force-pushing.
- [x] Source, focused suites, full build, and strict MXC proof passed on the final local head.
- [x] Failed-first official beta.2 behavior is documented rather than masked.
- [ ] Fresh GitHub CI on the updated head.
- [ ] OpenClaw wizard-runtime fix https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110382 reviewed/landed, or beta package updated with an equivalent fix.
- [ ] Maintainer approval of the beta-default release contract.

This PR is ready for review as the Windows Companion side of the beta integration. It should not merge as a claim that unmodified official beta.2 already passes the complete setup path.

## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Sanitized operator/agent engineering record</summary>

- This PR was developed across a multi-day operator/agent recovery and validation effort, not as a mechanical version bump.
- The operator required the Windows Companion to remain the owner of WSL creation, service lifecycle, Windows Node, and MXC, while OpenClaw remains the owner of the native onboarding wizard.
- Early attempts exposed a stale release target, culture-sensitive compact-number formatting, wizard reconnect failures, pairing/revocation ordering problems, and test-harness flakes. Each accepted in-scope issue was corrected and rerun instead of being hidden with sleeps, disabled tests, or a custom production installer.
- The release target moved to official OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.2` after that beta became available. The branch was then integrated with the latest Windows Node `main`, preserving newer upstream pairing and telemetry fixes rather than duplicating them.
- Official beta.2 installed through the real Companion-owned WSL path but lost the Gateway during the native wizard. Investigation isolated the defect to OpenClaw's Gateway wizard runtime, not the Companion installer.
- A separate, narrow OpenClaw correction was built and packaged. The Companion test harness first installed official beta.2 normally, then injected the corrected package only in the disposable proof distro. That correction is not hidden in this PR.
- Final-head automated proof passed: Connection `443/443`, SetupEngine `448/448`, Tray `1742/1742`, Shared `2866` plus `31` explicit integration skips.
- Final-head supported-path proof passed: revocation/reconnect `1/1`; strict Gateway-to-Windows-Node-to-MXC `2/2`, including a protected-write denial; both runs uninstalled and removed their temporary WSL distros.
- Final Auto-review reported one restart/uninstall concern. Direct call-path inspection showed the claimed uninstall branch does not exist in the restart helper, so no speculative code was added.
- No operator secrets, tokens, private messages, raw prompts, or runtime data are included in this transcript.

</details>

target.title: Add Tailscale Serve support for WSL gateways
target.body: ## Summary - Problem: Generated WSL gateways are loopback-only, so Companion cannot use a private tailnet endpoint. - Why it matters: Users with Tailscale need secure remote access without LAN exposure, port forwarding, or localhost fallback. - What changed: Added opt-in Tailscale Serve provisioning, browser/auth-key authorization, WSS gateway registration, Tailscale-aware recovery, runtime checks, redaction, and docs. - User impact: New/replacement generated gateways can publish privately at `wss://..ts.net`. Tailscale identity authentication is a separate explicit opt-in. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): No Funnel, Headscale, Tailscale SSH, subnet routing, named services, Windows Tailscale installation/removal, or in-place upgrades of existing gateways. Tailscale lifecycle and Serve remain root-owned; the `openclaw` account is not a Tailscale operator. ## Change Type (select all) - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [x] Docs / instructions - [x] Tests / validation - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore / infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Tray / WinUI UX - [ ] Windows node capability - [ ] Local MCP / `winnode` - [x] Gateway / connection / pairing - [x] Setup / onboarding - [x] Permissions / privacy / security - [x] Tests / CI / docs ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #966 - [ ] Related to a bug or regression ## Validation Current commit: `4a70b196 Scope Tailscale recovery to managed gateways` - `.\build.ps1` - Passed: Shared, CLI, WinNode CLI, SetupEngine, and WinUI builds. - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore` - Passed: 448, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0. - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` - Passed: 2724, Failed: 0, Skipped: 31. - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` - Passed: 1671, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0. - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore --filter FullyQualifiedName~ConnectionPageTailscaleRecoveryTests` - Passed: 4, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0. - `git diff --check` - Passed. ## Real behavior proof ### Current-head automated proof The current head includes focused regression coverage for the security and failure boundaries requested in review: - happy-path Serve finalization: exact HTTPS proxy target, device-pair public URL write, WSS endpoint publication, and root-owned Serve operation; - browser/HTTPS approval polling until configured or bounded timeout; - Serve health-check failure rolls back Funnel/Serve state, logs out, and disables `tailscaled` before pairing; - Tailscale transport with identity trust off keeps `gateway.auth.allowTailscale=false` and preserves shared/bootstrap/device-token precedence; - Tailscale-disabled fresh and replacement pipelines skip only Tailscale steps; - Funnel detection rejects public exposure and surfaces recovery guidance; cleanup resets Funnel and Serve before daemon teardown. ### Current-head WinUI managed vs. unmanaged Tailscale recovery proof - Environment tested: Windows 11 with two isolated Companion profiles. Each profile used a deliberately non-resolving fake `wss://[redacted].ts.net` endpoint; no real tailnet hostname, credential, or WSL gateway was used. - PR head / commit tested: `4a70b196 Scope Tailscale recovery to managed gateways`. - Exact steps: 1. Started Companion with an app-owned record marked `IsLocal=true` and `SetupManagedDistroName=OpenClawGateway-Proof`, then allowed the fake WSS connection to fail. 2. Repeated with an external/manual `.ts.net` record without a managed-distro marker. - Live WinUI diagnostic: - The managed record visibly rendered **Tailscale gateway unavailable** and **Check Tailscale access**, including the Windows sign-in, same-tailnet, `tailscaled`, Serve, OpenClaw service, Funnel, WSS-only, and no-localhost-fallback guidance. - The manual/external record visibly rendered **Can't reach gateway** and only the ordinary gateway-host, network/VPN, and SSH-tunnel recovery guidance. It did not display the Tailscale-specific recovery path. - Observed result: Dedicated Tailscale recovery is scoped to app-owned generated WSL gateways; external/manual `.ts.net` gateways retain ordinary network recovery. ### Current-head live Windows/WSL/Tailscale proof - Environment tested: Windows host with WSL2 and Windows Tailscale connected to the same tailnet as the replacement `OpenClawGateway` distro. - PR head / commit tested: `4a70b196 Scope Tailscale recovery to managed gateways`. - Setup result: generated app-owned record is `wss://…ts.net`, named `Tailscale (OpenClawGateway)`, marked local, and retains the managed distro association. It has no shared or bootstrap token. - Tailscale state: Windows and WSL MagicDNS suffixes matched; `tailscaled` was active as root; the non-root `openclaw` user gateway service was active and could run `tailscale whois`. - Serve and public exposure: Windows HTTPS to the generated hostname returned `200`; `tailscale serve status --json` contained exactly one `127.0.0.1:18789` proxy; neither Serve nor `tailscale funnel status --json` reported a public Funnel flag. - Identity trust: `gateway.auth.allowTailscale=true`. A Windows-originated WSS `connect` with no shared/bootstrap/device-token fields and no device identity reached `NOT_PAIRED / DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`, rather than token authorization rejection. The same token-free request with the already-paired device's signed identity returned `ok: true`. This proves the intended layered path: Serve-verified tailnet identity plus normal paired-device identity, without silently falling back to a shared token. - Companion result: `openclaw nodes status` reported one paired and connected node; `openclaw nodes invoke --command device.info --params '{}'` returned `ok: true` through the WSS record. - Redaction: setup logs contained zero `tskey-` matches and zero `login.tailscale.com` authorization URLs. - Screenshot/artifact links verified? - - Not verified / blocked: A fresh destructive rollback/uninstall execution was intentionally not repeated after the successful live setup, to preserve the working gateway. The current-head rollback and cleanup paths are covered by the focused automated tests above. Funnel, Headscale, Tailscale SSH, subnet routing, and named Tailscale Services remain intentionally out of scope. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes`) - Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes`) - New/changed network calls? (`Yes`) - Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`) - Data access scope changed? (`No`) - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: - Private Serve is opt-in and OpenClaw remains loopback-bound inside WSL. - `tailscale up`, Serve, reset, logout, and daemon administration are root-owned. The gateway account receives no Tailscale operator authority. - Tailscale identity trust is separately opt-in. When enabled, verified tailnet identity and tailnet ACLs become part of the gateway authorization boundary; token/device credentials remain available. - Auth keys are transient, never accepted through CLI arguments or persisted config, and setup logs redact auth keys and Tailscale authorization URLs. - Funnel is unsupported, detected, and rejected. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? (`Yes`) - Config/env changes? (`Yes`) - Migration needed? (`No`) - Existing managed gateways remain unchanged. To opt in, create or replace an app-generated WSL gateway and enable **Tailnet access with Tailscale Serve**. - Optional headless inputs: `--tailscale`, `--tailscale-trust-auth`, `--tailscale-auth browser|auth-key`, `--tailscale-hostname`, and `OPENCLAW_SETUP_TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY` for auth-key mode. ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.
